title: Shortest Travel Times Between Every Station Pair
real_world_story: A transit network serves many stations and the system frequently needs the shortest travel time between different pairs. To answer these quickly, the system precomputes the shortest travel time between every pair of stations so any future query can be answered instantly.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A weighted graph of stations with connections and travel times
real_world_connection.query_represents: A frequent request about the shortest travel time between two stations
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Precomputing all-pairs shortest travel times in advance

problem_statement: Given a weighted, undirected graph with N stations, an adjacency matrix where a positive value represents the travel time between two directly connected stations and 0 represents no direct connection, compute the shortest travel time between every pair of stations. Then answer Q queries, each asking for the shortest travel time between two stations.
task: Precompute all-pairs shortest travel times and answer each query with the minimum travel time.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The next N lines each contain N integers forming the adjacency matrix (0 on the diagonal, positive integer travel time between directly connected stations, 0 for no direct connection). The next line contains an integer Q. The next Q lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a query.
output_format: For each query, print the minimum travel time between station U and station V. If they are not connected, print -1.

examples.explanation: The shortest time from station 1 to station 4 is via station 2: 1 + 2 = 3. From station 2 to station 3 it is 1 + 2 + 1 = 3 via station 4, and the shortest time from a station to itself is 0.

expected_algorithm.name: Floyd-Warshall
expected_algorithm.reason: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest distance between every pair of nodes in O(N^3), allowing many queries to be answered in constant time afterward.

hint: Start with a distance matrix initialized to the direct connection weights.
For each intermediate station K, check whether traveling through K shortens any pair travel time.
Update the matrix until every pair holds its shortest travel time.
real_world_takeaway: Precomputing all-pairs travel times lets a transit system answer large numbers of journey queries instantly instead of recomputing each one separately.
